cells.tense: You are giving shape to what a group keeps and repeats, right now.
cells.ask: Offer one small way of doing something the group needs, and let people use it without you having to keep it.
cells.core:
Right now you're giving shape to what a group keeps and repeats. Not the one talking over the room and not the one sitting it out — you build the frame that lets the important things travel. A meeting runs on it. A practice survives because you held its edges. People settle around you when the shape is clear and you're not standing over it.

The frame is worth keeping light. What you build next should serve the thing it holds rather than becoming the thing itself. Let something small pass through your hands and out into the group without you needing to own it. Then the structure stays a container, and the group can carry it without you in the room.
cells.sheetLine: You give shape to what the group keeps and passes on.
cells.verb: Building the frame that lets what matters be carried forward.
cells.place: In the shared life of a group, among the forms people inherit and pass down.

cells.tense: You will keep tightening the form until it can't carry anything at all.
cells.ask: Pick one routine you've been holding tightly and loosen it today — let another person decide how it goes.
cells.core:
A frame people can lean on is what this is for: the shape clear, carrying what matters, holding without anyone standing over it. That's what's available here. What's happening instead is the tightening. Something hasn't gone wrong yet, and the wall to stop it is already up. The form you made to hold a thing has become the thing you serve, and it takes more of your day than the work does.

Look at one routine you keep and ask who it's actually for. The structure doesn't have to go. Step back far enough to see what the shape is for, and let that clarity reach this one before you tighten it again.
cells.sheetLine: You're protecting the frame instead of the thing it was built to hold.
cells.verb: Building the frame that lets what matters be carried forward.
cells.place: In the shared life of a group, among the forms people inherit and pass down.

cells.tense: You stopped at a doorway that had already closed behind you, and you're still standing there.
cells.ask: Take one task that feels stuck, write down the single next physical step, and do only that step today.
cells.core:
A mess can be handed shape: sorted into what belongs together, put in an order that holds, passed to others so the thing moves. That's the work when it's running well here. What's not running is the sequencing. The pieces won't line up — not because you don't care, but because the frame that used to hold them isn't there anymore. You're standing where order used to be, waiting for it to come back on its own, and the pile keeps growing.

Start with one stuck thing and find its smallest next step. Write that step down, do only that, and the ground clears for something that actually holds.
cells.sheetLine: The old structure is gone and you're waiting for it to come back.
cells.verb: Building the frame that lets what matters be carried forward.

cells.tense: You are holding the shape of this group while telling yourself you are just getting through.
cells.ask: Name one pattern you've been keeping for a group, out loud, and say that you're the one keeping it.
cells.core:
People copy how you do things. They wait to see what the group will repeat, and it gets decided — by how you show up, by what you let pass and what you stop. You call it just getting through the day. The shape is yours, and it's holding. With the hand visible, the same thing reads clearly: you set the form, you say what it's for, and people build on it because they know whose it is.

Some of what you keep came in before you could choose it, and letting it end is allowed. The first move is to say what's yours. One pattern you've been maintaining for the group — name it as something you do.
cells.sheetLine: The shape is yours. You just haven't claimed it.
cells.verb: Building the frame that lets what matters be carried forward.
cells.place: In the shared life of a group, among the forms people inherit and pass down.
